note: Self-employed in the hospitality and restaurant business, so successful is a qualified match on occupation. Good-to-great is the cleanest match in the batch and came from his own mouth - 'I would say that I'm on average level right now, but I can feel that I can do better' - after the rep described the segment to him. He is plainly not deconditioned at 36, training three to four times a week for two years. The misses are the two that decided the call. Income failed on contact: he found $4,000 for three months expensive and had not expected the programme to cost what it does. And health is emphatically not his neglected area - he trains consistently, has effectively stopped drinking, and takes protein, creatine, vitamin D and omega. That is the ICP's own paradox in a single call: he matches the good-to-great criterion perfectly and, precisely because nothing is wrong, there was nothing for the offer to solve. It is worth recording alongside the sales manager's internal finding the same week that this exact segment converts worst - 'they don't see a big enough value' - because this prospect is that finding demonstrated live, and the rep's response was to reduce the price four times rather than build a gap.
